summary: Verified new priority-driven resolution workflow end-to-end. Backend pytest: 48/48 passing (5 new TestDispatchWorkflow cases added on top of the 43 existing regression tests). RSA dispatch on a HIGH incident sets resolution_path='rsa', status='in_progress', persists rsa{unit,eta_min,agent,dispatched_at}, appends timeline note, and is visible to customer via GET /api/incidents/{id}. Remote-then-slot flow on a LOW incident sets resolution_path='remote' (in_progress) and then, with remote_failed=true, resolution_path='slot' (assigned) with appointment{slot_start, slot_end, technician_name, position, lane, lanes_total=3, duration_min}. Queue auto-adjust verified: booking a Medium slot after an already-booked Low slot correctly places Medium at a position <= Low (priority High>Med>Low). Resolving (PATCH status=resolved) triggers recompute_slots and the remaining low slot stays valid. Lanes distribution across d_metro's 3 technicians verified by booking 4 low slots and confirming lanes_total=3 always and >=2 distinct lanes were used. Invalid dispatch mode -> 400. Frontend (Playwright + real backend): HIGH incident detail shows ONLY dispatch-rsa-btn (rsa=True, remote=False, slot=False); clicking it displays 'RSA dispatched · RSA Rapid Unit · ETA 45m' and timeline note appears. LOW incident detail shows try-remote-btn + book-slot-btn (rsa=False, remote=True, slot=True); clicking book-slot triggers toast 'Service slot booked & customer notified' and detail card renders 'Service slot booked' with 'queue #13 of 3 bays' and technician name. Customer /dashboard (session_token cookie): opening the LOW incident shows the customer-service-update card with 'Appointment booked for 9/21/2026, 1:00:00 PM with Ravi Kumar. You're #13 in the queue (3 service bays running).' and opening the HIGH incident shows 'Roadside Assistance is on the way — RSA Rapid Unit, ETA 45 minutes.' Full regression suite (auth, AI triage, photo upload, dealer ops assign/status/priority/escalate/resolve, KPIs, Connect sim, chat, callbacks pending/scheduled/past, cron auth+flip, recordings, per-branch scoping, dealerships listing) all still pass.
critical_code_review_comments: recompute_slots (server.py:617) reloads *all* non-resolved slot incidents for the dealership and rewrites every appointment on every dispatch or resolve. For a busy dealership this is O(N) per call and rewrites timestamps that were already communicated to customers, causing appointments to silently shift in the customer's UI. Consider only appending new bookings and only reshuffling when a higher-priority booking or resolution actually requires it, and emit a timeline note whenever an existing appointment moves so the customer sees why their slot changed.

notify_customer_appointment is fired on the initial slot booking only (dispatch endpoint). When recompute_slots later moves a customer's appointment (e.g. a higher-priority incident jumps ahead), no email/in-app notification is sent — the customer only sees the new time if they refresh /dashboard. Fire notify_customer_appointment for every incident whose appointment.slot_start changed inside recompute_slots.

dispatch endpoint accepts mode='remote' but there is no explicit path to mark remote as *succeeded* (only remote_failed=true -> slot). Currently the dealer has to PATCH status=resolved manually, which bypasses any 'remote fix succeeded' timeline note. Consider a mode='remote_success' or a dedicated resolve-via-remote button.

SERVICE_DURATION_MIN and BUSINESS_START_HOUR/END_HOUR are hardcoded module constants and shared across all dealerships. Different branches may have different working hours or bay capacities; consider persisting these on the dealership document.

Business hours are enforced in UTC (BUSINESS_START_HOUR=9, END=18). For a real-world deployment this means a dealership in IST would open at 14:30 local — flag for productisation; per-dealership timezone should be stored.

dispatch endpoint does not gate on current status. A HIGH incident that has already been resolved can still be RSA-dispatched (moving status back to in_progress). Add a guard: if status in {'resolved','closed'} -> 400.

recompute_slots ignores the appointment.duration_min already stored and always recomputes from SERVICE_DURATION_MIN[priority]. If a dealer manually changes priority after booking, the technician's downstream slot durations shift retroactively — arguably correct but should be surfaced in timeline.
